DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Date of Discharge: 22 March 2025
Patient Name: George Hassan
Date of Birth: 25/07/1960
Hospital Number: 63355343

Presenting Complaint
Attended the emergency department following a syncopal episode, described as a brief loss of consciousness preceded by dizziness. No associated chest pain, palpitations, or neurological symptoms reported.

Diagnosis
Essential Hypertension

Hospital Course
On admission, blood pressure was noted to be significantly elevated at 158/96 mmHg. Subsequent readings remained high. A comprehensive work-up including ECG, routine bloods (U&Es, FBC), and a clinical examination was performed. ECG showed normal sinus rhythm with no acute ischaemic changes. Blood results were within normal limits. The syncopal episode was attributed to a transient vasovagal event, with the underlying hypertension identified as a primary concern requiring management.

The patient was commenced on Ramipril 2.5mg once daily. Blood pressure response was monitored and found to be satisfactory, with readings improving to approximately 140/88 mmHg prior to discharge. The patient was educated on the diagnosis of hypertension, the importance of medication adherence, and lifestyle modifications including dietary salt reduction and regular physical activity.

Medications on Discharge
1. Ramipril 2.5mg once daily

Allergies
No known drug allergies.

Follow-Up Plan
To arrange a follow-up appointment with his General Practitioner in 2 weeks for a blood pressure check and medication review. Advised to monitor for any side effects of Ramipril, including cough or dizziness, and to report these to his GP. To continue with lifestyle modification advice provided during admission.

Discharged to
Home, in a stable condition.

Dr. Osei
Consultant Cardiologist
